title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
statement:
You are given two strings, `haystack` and `needle`, both made of lowercase English letters, where `needle` is never longer than `haystack`. Return the index of the first character of the earliest occurrence of `needle` as a contiguous block inside `haystack`. If `needle` does not occur in `haystack`, return `-1`.

For example, when `haystack` is `"butterfly"` and `needle` is `"fly"`, the answer is `6`, the index of the `f`.

Constraints: `1 <= haystack.length <= 200` and `1 <= needle.length <= haystack.length`.

constraints: Function signature: `function solve(haystack: string, needle: string)`.
Inputs are JSON-serializable values satisfying the bounds stated above.
hints: Write the honest O(n*m) version first: for every start position, compare characters and stop at the first mismatch.
After a mismatch the naive scan forgets everything it just matched; ask how much of the matched prefix is still a valid prefix of the pattern.
Precompute for each prefix of needle the length of the longest proper prefix that is also a suffix, and jump back to that length on a mismatch instead of restarting.

editorial.approach: The brute force tries each start position from 0 to `n - m` and compares characters until a mismatch or the end of `needle`, which costs O(n*m) time in the worst case and uses no auxiliary space. The optimal version is KMP: first build the prefix-function array of `needle` in O(m) by tracking, for each position, the length of the longest proper prefix that is also a suffix; then scan `haystack` once, and on a mismatch fall back to `fail[j - 1]` instead of restarting. The haystack pointer only ever moves forward, so the search is O(n) and the whole solution O(n + m) with O(m) extra space.
editorial.why_optimal: Every algorithm must read at least the part of `haystack` that it matches, so Ω(n) is a hard floor, and Ω(m) is needed just to read the pattern; KMP hits O(n + m) with a single forward pass and a failure table of size m. The naive scan is fast enough at `haystack.length <= 200`, but it degrades to O(n*m) on adversarial inputs such as a long run of `a` followed by a mismatch, which is exactly what the failure table eliminates.
editorial.pitfalls: The start loop must run while `start + m <= n`; using `start < n` reads past the end of `haystack`. In the prefix-function construction the fallback inside the while loop is `fail[j - 1]`, not `fail[i - 1]`, and `fail[0]` must stay 0. A match found at haystack index `i` starts at `i - m + 1`, a classic off-by-one when reporting the answer. The construction loop begins at `i = 1`, so a single-character `needle` never enters it and must still work through the search loop alone - verify that case explicitly. An empty `needle` is a match at index 0 and the KMP variant must return 0 explicitly, because its search loop would otherwise report the first position as a match of length 0.
